## Biography

I am an undergraduate student in Genomic Sciences at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), campus Cuernavaca. My academic interests focus on genomics, evolution, bioinformatics, and molecular biology.

Throughout my academic training, I have completed coursework in R, Python, and Bash, as well as in core biological disciplines such as evolutionary biology, molecular biology, genetics, and cell biology. This interdisciplinary foundation has allowed me to integrate computational approaches with biological theory, developing analytical workflows for biological data interpretation and working with large-scale genomic datasets.

My interests also extend to paleogenomics, regenerative medicine, and the biotechnological production of bioactive metabolites from plants and microorganisms. I am particularly motivated by the intersection of biology and computation, aiming to better understand the evolutionary and molecular mechanisms underlying complex biological systems and contribute to innovative applications in biotechnology and medicine.
